subject.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty

question: After the 200-post request defect is repaired, should cold Mattermost thread recovery keep the proposed awaited five-second, one-attempt-per-session policy?
rationale: The implementation deliberately trades first-turn latency and recovery from transient fetch failures against avoiding repeated REST delays; tests cannot determine which user-facing availability policy the Mattermost plugin should own.

options.title: Accept bounded one-attempt recovery
options.body: Clamp or paginate the request, retain the five-second one-attempt-per-session behavior, and explicitly accept the first-turn latency and no-retry tradeoff.

options.title: Add cooldown-based retry
options.body: Repair the page limit and allow a later bounded retry after transient failure without retrying every inbound turn.

options.title: Pause server-side recovery
options.body: Do not merge the backfill until a different non-blocking recovery design is agreed.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded one-attempt recovery
recommendation.body: Clamp or paginate the request, retain the five-second one-attempt-per-session behavior, and explicitly accept the first-turn latency and no-retry tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the closest persisted Mattermost thread-context behavior and its routing semantics.
